answers.answer: Reveal a region card for the King. Each player takes another region card as their home region and places their Grande there. Each starts with ten Caballeros: two in the home region beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
answers.evidence: Setup: reveal a region card for the King; each player takes another for home. Setup: “two” home, “one” on success track, “seven” in court.

answers.answer: In round 1, players choose who begins. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round begins. Others play clockwise. No power-card value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Players choose who begins” in round 1; later “player who took the last turn”; others play “clockwise”; no value already played may be matched.

answers.answer: Players take turns in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the Caballero allowance pictured on your power card from provinces to court. Recruitment happens before choosing an action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “descending power-card value”; “At the start of your turn recruit up to” the pictured number; afterward choose an action card.

answers.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King's region and Castillo cannot supply pieces for recruitment.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “you may take your own from the board to make up the difference”; “King's region remains taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.”

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment is from court to regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo. The allowance may be divided freely among destinations. The printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: Actions: allowance is a “maximum”; move from court to adjacent regions and/or Castillo, “dividing the allowance freely.”

answers.answer: Yes. Complete ordinary deployment and the special action in either order, one whole activity at a time; neither may be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Do them in either order,” “complete one activity before starting the other,” neither split or interleaved; may decline special action.

answers.answer: After a turn, set the selected action card aside so later players cannot choose it. At the end of the round, discard any remaining face-up action cards. The King card is revealed again each round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: selected card laid aside; discard remaining face-up cards after all players; King card “revealed again every round and never permanently discarded.”

answers.answer: Caballeros, Grandes, and mobile scoreboards may not move into or out of the King's region. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out; region may still be scored; moving King changes protected region.

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros you put in the Castillo. The King's location does not restrict entry. Castillo Caballeros cannot leave except during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: Caballeros may go into Castillo “regardless of the King's location”; “Announce clearly how many”; leave only during general scoring.

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: players secretly select one destination each for all their Castillo Caballeros, face down, before uncovering it; score the Castillo; reveal disks and move all Castillo Caballeros to their selected destinations (or court for an illegal King's-region selection), then replace Castillo empty; score the nine regions in scoring-track order and record points.
answers.evidence: General scoring: timing after rounds 3, 6, 9; four ordered stages begin with secretly choosing destinations “before uncovering the Castillo,” then score Castillo, reveal and empty it, then score nine regions.

answers.answer: A player must send all their Castillo Caballeros to one region, not split them, and may not choose the King's region. They cannot keep any in the Castillo. If they illegally selected the King's region, their pieces go to their court instead.
answers.evidence: General scoring: all Castillo Caballeros go to “one” region; choosing King's region prohibited; none may be retained or split; illegal selection sends pieces to court.

answers.answer: The three tied players each score 3 points (the second-place value); the player with three scores 1 point. Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.
answers.evidence: Region ranks example: 5/3/1 counts 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1. “Only Caballeros count”; Grande contributes zero Caballeros.

answers.answer: The players with 4, 3, and 2 Caballeros score 6, 4, and 0 respectively; the other player with 2 also scores 0.
answers.evidence: Publisher scoring example: on 6/4/2, counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: In a two-player game only first place can pay; in a three-player game first and second can pay. A tie for first between two players in a two-player game shifts to second place, which is outside the payable ranks, so neither scores.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: “Two players: only first place can pay”; “Three players: only first and second”; cutoff after rank shift means a two-player tie for first pays neither.

answers.answer: When the relevant region is scored, including on special scoring, the sole majority holder gets the King's bonus of +2 in the King's region and the home bonus of +2 if they have their own Grande there. Neither bonus applies on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Region ranks and bonuses: bonuses apply whenever relevant region scored, including special scoring; each is +2 for sole holder; neither awarded on tie for first.

answers.answer: Special scoring reveals and scores Castillo contents, then covers the same pieces again. It does not empty or redistribute them; redistribution waits for general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: special scoring reveals and scores contents, then covers them again without redistribution; Stack 3 Castillo: cover the same Caballeros.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King's region, the two scoreboards cannot be stacked, and neither may be reversed or rotated to change its values.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: “Castillo is allowed”; no movement into or out of King's region; cannot be stacked; use right side up, never reversed or rotated.

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region, excluding the King's region and Castillo; it cannot leave the King's region. The destination may already contain several Grandes. It becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: another region except King's region or Castillo; cannot leave King's region; destination may contain several Grandes; destination becomes new home.

answers.answer: The recovery action returns any one of your played power cards, including the one played that turn. You need not reveal which card you take, though taking the visible top card will be apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: return any one played card “including the one played this turn”; “You need not reveal which.”

answers.answer: The standard game ends after completing all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins.
answers.evidence: Overview and End: game ends after third general scoring, not before final regions score; furthest along success track wins.

answers.answer: Separate the action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place them face down. Reveal the top card of each of the five stacks at the start of each round. The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup: stacks by 1–5, shuffle separately; Turn Structure: reveal top card of each of five stacks; marker starts at 1.

answers.answer: No. Played power cards remain in each player's face-up used stack, with only its top card visible, rather than returning to hand. A special action can recover one.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: played cards remain in face-up used stack with “only the top card visible,” rather than returning to hand; special action can recover a played card.

answers.answer: If the King card's special action happens before deployment, the King's new position determines adjacency for deployment. The King may be placed in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: moving King before ordinary deployment means use “new position”; Stack 5 King: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: Keep the Veto card before you to stop one special action during this round or the next. It cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion of an action card.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: retain card to stop one special action during this or next round; cannot stop ordinary deployment.

answers.answer: While holding Veto, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: you may stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete action. A completed action cannot be vetoed; already executed parts are not undone.
answers.evidence: Veto: players announce special actions; object as soon as player starts; can stop before execution or remaining part of incomplete action; completed actions cannot be vetoed and executed parts are not undone.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Veto: “Discard after using the veto once”; if unused, discard at “end of the next round.”

answers.answer: All fellow players, but not the selecting player, send all Caballeros in their courts to the provinces. A fellow player with an empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros to provinces; empty court sends none; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends both to the provinces; you, as selecting player, are unaffected and keep your five.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — three from court: fellow player sends three or all they have if fewer than three; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed execution paragraph and matching card face require each player, including the selecting player, to send three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Starting with the player to the selecting player's left, players proceed clockwise, with the selecting player last. Pieces may come from any regions and/or court, but never the King's region or Castillo. The heading instead says “fellow players.” No explicit shortfall rule is supplied.
answers.evidence: The King returns: detailed paragraph/card say each player including selector sends three; left then clockwise, selector last; any regions/court except King's region/Castillo; heading says fellow players; no shortfall rule.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each piece to its owner's provinces. Pieces cannot come from courts, the King's region, or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one for each player including self; return to owner's provinces; no taking from courts, King's region or Castillo.

answers.answer: Affected fellow players simultaneously choose one region secretly on their disks and reveal together. Each must choose a region containing at least two of their Caballeros, and two are returned to the provinces.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove two: choices simultaneous and revealed together; choose a region with at least two; return two to provinces.

answers.answer: If they have at most one Caballero in every region, choose a region containing one and return that one Caballero to the provinces.
answers.evidence: Secret removal fallback: if player has at most one in every region, choose a region with one and return that one.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses a region with at least one of their own Caballeros on a disk; choices are revealed together. They return all their own Caballeros there to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove all: simultaneous secret disk selection, reveal together; choose region with at least one, return all own there; player with none is unaffected.

answers.answer: Yes, the acting player may choose any region, including the King's region, or the Castillo. Apply normal region-scoring rules, rank limits, and bonuses. If Castillo is scored, cover the same pieces again; do not redistribute them.
answers.evidence: Pick one region to score: any region including King's region or Castillo; normal rules, rank limits and bonuses; Castillo contents covered without redistribution.

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia (4/2/0), Catalonia (4/2/1), and Seville (4/3/1). Eligibility depends on the current first value: Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify, while Granada with 4/0/0 does. Applicable bonuses apply to special scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 all 4: current first value is 4; printed group listed; mobile 8/4/0 in Galicia removes it and 4/0/0 in Granada adds it; special scoring bonuses apply.

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country, Aragon, and Valencia; the 6-and-7 group is Old Castile, New Castile, and Granada. Eligibility uses the current first value, so mobile scoreboards can remove or add regions to these groups. Castillo is not included in all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3: all 5 current first value 5 and named group; “Castillo is not scored.” All 6- and 7-value current first 6 or 7 and named group; mobile scoreboard replaces printed values.

answers.answer: Only sole first places score; tied leaders score nothing because they would normally receive second place. All lower ranks also score nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 first-position only: only sole first places score; tie for first scores nothing; other ranks get nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Both tied board regions are scored. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more Caballeros.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 most: score all regions tied for most; Castillo is neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions and score all tied for the least. Empty regions are excluded, as is the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 least: compare nonempty board regions; score all tied for least; empty regions and Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each secretly chooses another region with a disk, then choices are revealed simultaneously and groups move there. If a player chooses the King's region or the vacated region, that player's pieces go to their court instead.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Movement: all fellow players move all own pieces out; secret disk choices revealed simultaneously; choosing King's region or vacated region sends pieces to court.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King to a neighboring region, at most one region away. The King card can place him in any region except Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Royal Adviser: neighboring region, no more than one away; Stack 5: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from provinces to your court. This is separate from the 4-stack card's ordinary deployment of up to four from court to the board; complete the two activities in either order.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 The Court: two own from provinces to court; separate from ordinary up-to-four deployment; either activity can go first.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose regions on their disks and reveal simultaneously. Each uniquely chosen region is scored under normal rules; any region chosen by multiple players is not scored.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: all players choose secretly and reveal simultaneously; uniquely chosen regions score; multiple selections mean region is not scored.

answers.answer: You take all your own Caballeros from one region and may distribute them among other regions and/or Castillo, returning some to the original region if desired. Origins exclude the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region but may include Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue all-own effect: take all from one region, distribute among other regions and/or Castillo; may return some to original. General Stack 1 rules exclude King's region and Castillo as origins, King region as destination.

answers.answer: Up to two additional own Caballeros may move from court, for up to three total including the normal deployment of one. The normal one must go adjacent to the King and/or Castillo; the additional two may go to any non-King region and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue two more from court: up to two additional; with normal one, up to three; only normal one requires adjacency; destinations as stated.

answers.answer: You choose one special alternative, not both: either two more from court or all your own from one region. The normal up-to-one deployment still applies.
answers.evidence: Intrigue choice: “Choose one” preceding special actions, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: Up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros may be moved from one origin region only, distributed to other non-King regions and/or Castillo. They cannot come from multiple origins.
answers.evidence: Intrigue up to five: own and/or foreign from one origin region to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move up to three foreign Caballeros from any non-King board regions, including multiple origins; your own pieces cannot be included. Castillo is forbidden as an origin but allowed as a destination; any non-King region is also a legal destination.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any three foreign: other players' only, from any non-King board regions, multiple origins, never Castillo; destinations any non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: The any-three action allows up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. The any-four action allows up to four own and/or foreign from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Stack 1 rules exclude Castillo as an origin and the King's region as origin or destination.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any three and any four table entries specify ownership, quantity and destinations; Stack 1 says all relocation origins exclude King's region and Castillo and destinations exclude King's region but may include Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros, as separate ownership allowances. They may come from any regions other than the King's region or Castillo; destinations may be any non-King region and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue two own and two foreign: up to two own plus two foreign; general Stack 1 rules exclude King's region and Castillo as origins and allow Castillo, not King's region, as destination.

answers.answer: Move up to four own Caballeros only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Castillo and the King's region cannot be origins; the King's region cannot be a destination.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any four of your own: up to four own only, from non-King origins into other non-King regions and/or Castillo; general origins exclude Castillo too.

answers.answer: The each-player secret-choice scoring card allows the King's region but not Castillo; unique selections score and duplicates do not. The separate pick-one-location card allows its acting player to choose any region, including both the King's region and Castillo; Castillo scoring covers the same pieces again without redistribution.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 secret scoring: disk includes nine regions including King's, not Castillo. Stack 2 pick one: any region including King's or Castillo; Castillo contents covered, not distributed.

answers.answer: The two mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. The special action may introduce one from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Components: two mobile scoreboards beside board; Stack 4 Mobile scoreboard: introduce from beside board or move one already on board.
